title: QuestHUDController.cs
summary: The UI Toolkit Quest Journal drawer: lists every active/completed Quest with live per-criterion progress, the episode countdown, and the Episode Complete / Game Over modal shown when a Quest resolves.

notes.match: public static QuestHUDController Instance { get; private set; }
notes.text: Singleton — Quest, PlayerControls, CollectiblesManager and NPCInteractionManager all reach this via QuestHUDController.Instance.
How often the quest list/timer repaint themselves — not every frame, to avoid rebuilding UI elements 60 times a second.
Public so other scripts (CollectiblesManager, NPCInteractionManager) can check 'is the journal open' to suppress their own prompts.

Cached references to every named element in the Quest HUD's UXML: the drawer itself, its 'closed' shortcut icon, the scrollable quest list, summary/timer labels, and the entire Episode Complete/Game Over modal's pieces.
Standard singleton Awake, plus resolving the shared PlayerInputBindings for the OpenQuest action.
On Start, ensures the UI is wired, forces the drawer closed (regardless of any serialized/edited state), and does an initial paint of the quest list.
Cleanup: unhooks the close button's handler, clears the questOpen flag, and releases the singleton so a fresh instance in a reloaded scene doesn't collide with a stale one.

notes.match: bool togglePressed = inputBindings != null && inputBindings.OpenQuest != null
notes.text: Prefers the actual OpenQuest input action; falls back to a raw Q key check only if that action wasn't resolved for some reason.
Won't toggle open while paused or mid-conversation — same 'only one full-screen system at a time' discipline as everywhere else.
The periodic repaint: only runs once every refreshInterval seconds using a countdown timer, not every single frame.
Same 'query every named UI Toolkit element once by name' pattern as BagUIController/PauseMenu, just against the Quest HUD's own UXML.
Public toggle, called by the HUD journal button and the Q key.
Opening closes Tasks first (same mutual-exclusion rule), flips the flags, and immediately refreshes so the list isn't stale from before it was opened.
Closing is the mirror image — note IsOpen/questOpen get cleared even if the drawer element itself is missing, so state never gets stuck out of sync with the visuals.
Recomputes which quests are 'visible' (active or completed — not ones that are simply inactive/not-yet-started) and how many of those are done, for the summary line.
Finds the first active quest that actually has a timer and shows its countdown; adds a warning CSS class in the last 10 seconds for a visual urgency cue.
Clears and rebuilds the entire quest list every refresh — simplest correct approach given the refresh interval is already throttled to a few times a second, well within UI Toolkit's rebuild budget.

Builds the card for one Quest (title, status, description and a row per requirement) and one progress row (BAG / STRESS / PERSON) as a VisualElement tree in code. It is mechanical, so it is not walked through here.
Two thin wrappers around a shared modal-builder: one for success, one for the timeout failure case, each supplying their own copy and primary/secondary button targets.

Fills in the modal's text and re-wires its two buttons' click handlers (carefully removing old handlers first so repeated calls don't stack), then shows it, forces the game into a paused-and-unlocked-cursor state, and freezes time.
Retry reloads the current scene through the episode loading screen (with the saved episode number), a clean way to fully reset all quest, collectible and NPC state.
Next Chapter persists the unlock + a 'start page' pref MainMenuController reads to jump straight to chapter select, then returns to the Main Menu scene.
Plain 'give up and return to menu' — resets the start page back to the very first Main Menu screen.
